column2: A Shudra-horse is impure, restless, dull, ill-formed, ill-minded, wicked; a horse held by the rein that shows saliva —
it should be engaged in the paces by the taking and releasing of the rein. I shall tell the marks of horses and the rest, as Shalihotra said.
With pippali and rock salt, with warm water it destroys colic. Ginger, ativisha, mustaka, sananta, bilva-malika —
a horse should drink a decoction of these, destroying all diarrhea. Goat's milk boiled with priyangu and sariva,
drunk with ample sugar, frees the horse from fatigue. In a trough an oil enema should be given to the horse;
the vein of the belly should be pierced; by that it becomes comfortable. Pomegranate, triphala, the three pungents and jaggery in equal parts —
this lump should be given to horses, destroying cough. The horse should drink vasaka juice with priyangu, lodhra and honey;
or milk with the five jujube-roots and the rest; it is freed from cough. In all cases of diseases at the shoulders, first purification is best;
by anointing and rubbing, oiling; the order of nasal medicines is remembered. For feverish horses the course of treatment is with milk alone.
Root of lodhra and kandhara, citron, agni and ginger; kushtha, hing, vacha, rasna — this paste destroys swelling.
Manjishtha, licorice, grapes, the two brihatis, red sandal, cucumber seeds and roots, shringataka and kasheruka —
this, boiled in goat's milk, well cooled, with sugar, drunk by a fasting horse, frees it from bloody urine.
Swelling of veins at the nape, jaw and throat, a throat seizure: anointing with pungent oil is praised there;
in throat-seizure disease, swelling mostly in the throat region: pratyakpushpi, agni, rock salt, sauras juice,
with krishna and hing, having made a nasal medicine one does not sink. Turmeric, jyotishmati, patha, krishna, kushtha, vacha, honey —
this paste with jaggery and urine in tongue-stiffness is beneficial. With sesame, yashti, turmeric and neem leaves combined,
with honey a cleansing ball; with ghee, wound-healing. Horses that go lame from injury, with severe pain,
for them a pouring treatment with oil removes pain quickly. In ripe or split wounds from aggravation of humors and injury, the wound regimen:
with pastes of ashvattha, udumbara, plaksha, madhuka and vata.
An abundance of water decoction, comfortably warm, cleanses a wound. Shatahva, ginger, rasna, manjishtha, kushtha and rock salt,
with devadaru, the pair of vacha, turmeric, red sandal, oil cooked with decoction of guduchi and with milk,
for rubbing and for enema and nasal medicine should be applied everywhere to the afflicted. Blood-letting by leeches at the eye-corner for one with eye disease;
treatment with decoction of udumbara and ashvattha bark; with amalaka, duralabha, tikta, priyangu and saffron in equal parts,
a paste made with guduchi is beneficial for hanging (disease). In swelling, stones, hardened and dry organ,
and in quickly acting fault, splitting at once is desired. Cow-dung, manjishtha, kushtha, turmeric, sesame and mustard,
ground with cow-urine, rubbing destroys itching. A cool decoction with honey in the nose with sugar,
by drinking removes blood-bile, and likewise ashvakarna. Salt should be given to horses every seventh day;
and to those who have eaten, vaaruni when overdrinking. With jivaniya herbs, sweet ones, grapes and sugar,
with pippali in autumn a drink with padmaka; with vidanga, pippali, dhanya, shatahva, lodhra and rock salt,
with chitraka — a drink for horses at the cold season's arrival; with lodhra, priyangu, kamusta, pippali and vishvabheshaja,
with honey, a drink in spring would destroy phlegm; with priyangu, pippali, lodhra, yashti, akshas and the great medicine,
in summer wine with jaggery should be given as a drink. Piercing is desired; lodhra-wood with salt, pippali and ginger,
joined with oil, these would be the drink in the rainy season. Those afflicted by bile aggravated in summer, those with enriched blood in autumn,
those with loosened excrement in the rains — horses should drink ghee; those with excess phlegm and wind should drink oil.
For those who have oil-complications, drying should be done; three days thin gruel without oil, and food with buttermilk.
In autumn and summer ghee; in cold and spring oil; in rains and cool season the double (oil and ghee) in enema is desired.
Heavy, moisture-causing foods, exercise, bathing and sunshine, and wind should be avoided; for a horse that has drunk oil these are forbidden.
Bathing, drinking and defecation of horses at the arrival of water; in very bad weather a single drink is praised;
in moderate cold and heat two drinks and one bath; in summer three baths and drinks and long immersion.
Four adhakas of husked barley should be given; one may also give chickpeas, rice, mudga or peas.
In a day and night ten tulas of green fodder, or eight of dry, or four of husk should be given.
Durva destroys bile; barley, cough; husk, accumulation of phlegm; arjuna, asthma; and so mana, loss of strength.
Diseases of wind, bile, phlegm and mixed humors will not trouble a horse that feeds on durva.
Two rope-bindings for the vicious on both flanks; behind, a bow should be made supported by a distant peg;
they should dwell in a spread-out place with fumigated ground, where fodder is laid and lamps kept and well guarded; cocks, goats and deer should be kept in the horse house.
Then four-streamed pots, and flags at fire and the other corners; four arches at the door; the elephants Airavata and the rest;
in the east and so on with herbs, a separate vessel for the gods; separately a hundred ghee oblations; having worshipped the elephants by circumambulation,
the elephant, fire, deities and the rest, the outsiders went to their own homes. One should give fees to Brahmins and horse-physicians and the rest.
Having mounted the she-elephant, the one who knows the time should speak in the ear: in the nectar of the king of elephants, having made peace, one should recite the mantra:
Thus consecrated the king should mount him at an auspicious time. Nine armed elephants should follow him;
in the hall, on the platform with a lotus drawn, he should worship outside the world-guardians and the rest; in the filaments the Strength, the elephant, the Earth and Sarasvati;
in the middle, having worshipped the drum with scents, garlands and ointments, having offered, a pot full of juices should be given to a Brahmin;

one should honor the elephant-chief, the elephant-keepers and the reckoner; that drum he should give to the elephant-chief and he too should sound it; with auspicious deep sounds, one at the hip should sound it.
Gorochana destroys poison and demons; the giver of fodder to cows goes to heaven; the man in whose house cows suffer goes to hell.
The giver of fodder to others' cows is a heaven-goer; one devoted to cows shares Brahma's world. By giving cows, praising them, protecting them, he lifts the family.
The earth is purified by the breath of cows; by touching them, sin is destroyed. Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curds, ghee and kusha water,
and a one-night fast would purify even a dog-cooker. For destruction of all evil, practiced of old by lords,
each of three days is remembered as the great Santapana. This fulfils all desires and crushes all evil.
Krichchhra-atikrichchhra with milk for twenty-one days: they become stainless, and with all desires attained, the best of cows (devotees) become bowed.
Three days one should drink hot urine; three days drink hot ghee; three days drinking hot milk; then three days living on air.
The Tapta-krichchhra vow destroys all sin and gives Brahma's world; with cold things it is Shita-krichchhra, told by Brahma, giving Brahma's world.
One should bathe with cow-urine and make a living from cow products; go with the cows, eat when they have eaten, a vower of the cow.
In one month he becomes sinless and a dweller in the cow-world, heaven-goer. Having recited the Gomati knowledge he goes to the supreme cow-world;
with songs and dances and Apsarases he rejoices there in an aerial car. Cows are ever fragrant; cows smell of guggulu;
cows are the foundation of beings; cows are the supreme blessing; cows are the best food, the best oblation of the gods;
purifying all beings, they flow and speak. With oblation purified by mantra they satisfy the immortals in heaven.
In the Agnihotras of sages, cows are employed in oblations; for all beings cows are the best refuge;
cows are the supreme purifier, cows the best auspiciousness; cows are the stairway to heaven, cows are fortunate and eternal.
Homage to the cows, the glorious, the Saurabheyis; homage to the Brahma-born, the pure ones; homage, homage.
Brahmins and cows are one family made twofold; in one the mantras stand, in the other the oblation stands.
